about: The outline of every named scene geometry, once. A scene node names its shape (data.geometry); emit/html-shapes.mjs
and emit/emit_pptx.py both draw the name from this table, so a polygonal geometry cannot be one outline in the HTML
page and another in the PowerPoint file. It was two hand-kept lists before - polygon points for HTML, an Office
preset for PowerPoint - and the presets were not the polygons: a preset notchedRightArrow's shaft is half its height,
a preset hexagon's or trapezoid's slant is a share of the shorter side rather than of the width, so a label measured
to sit inside the HTML shape ran out of the PowerPoint one.
outlines: one closed polygon per geometry, points in the unit square of the node's frame (x across, y down).
A coordinate is a number, or a pair [a, b] meaning a + b * (shorter side of the frame / this axis's length): the
way an outline says 'half the shorter side', which is how a chevron's point keeps its angle on a wide band.
presets: the few geometries PowerPoint draws as its own autoshape (so the shape keeps its name and its yellow
handle when edited by hand) because the preset's outline at these adjustments IS the polygon above at every frame.
Each is proved by evals/tests/test_shape_outlines.py, which computes the preset's path from its PresentationML
definition and compares it with the outline. A geometry not listed here is written as a freeform of the outline;
list one only with that proof.
